messages:
sofia: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A about engineering process (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). Two quick asks up front: where is the canonical release calendar, and how do Dedicated launches affect oncall rotations?

devon: calendar is in the engops group repo — link: https://go/internal/eng-release-calendar (perm: engops + product). I can add the Dedicated capacity milestones there by EOD.

maria: +1 on the calendar link. Also: for Dedicated launches, do we require a longer canary window or a different error-budget threshold?

ajay: short answer: longer canary by default. Proposal we discussed in the meeting: 
- Dedicated production features get a 72h canary (vs 24h for hosted).
- Error budget trigger: >1.5x baseline error rate sustained for 30m OR >2% user-facing errors for 15m -> escalate and consider rollback.

kevin: can we make that configurable per-customer? big customers want stricter SLOs sometimes.

ajay: yes — default is param-driven. We store rollout_policy in the model-deploy config: 
```
rollout_policy: {
  canary_hours: 72,
  error_budget_pct: 2.0,
  alert_window_mins: 15
}
```
You can override per-dedicated-deployment.

sofia: Good. How will oncall handoff change when we have Dedicated spikes (e.g., model warmups)? Do we need separate SRE/infra rota for Dedicated vs Hosted?

devon: suggestion: single oncall with Dedicated tag routing — first responder triages and then pages Dedicated infra SME if the tag exists. We don't want two full rotas for now.

maria: operationally that seems fine, but we should update the runbook with explicit tagging rules. Example: if incident contains "dedicated" or customer_id -> notify Dedicated SME channel.

oncall-bot: Reminder: rotation swap scheduled for 2024-06-12 18:00 UTC — dev-oncall -> dev-sre (auto-posted from rota service).

kevin: small ask — can we add an automated smoke test after Dedicated deploys that validates 99th percentile latency < 1.5x baseline? If it fails, auto-halt rollout.

ajay: agree. We already have a smoke harness. I'll add the check to the rollout step: 
```
post_deploy_checks:
  - smoke_latency_p99 < 1.5 * baseline
  - correctness_evals.pass_rate >= 98
```
If checks fail then stop and notify #release-war-room.

sofia: Nice. Who owns the documentation updates? I can own the runbook editing but want SMEs to review.

devon: I'll PR the calendar entries and link to the runbook. Assigning review to @ajay and @maria.

maria: happy to review. Can we also add a short checklist in the all-hands notes for product PMs to confirm dedicated prerequisites (KMS, VPC, compliance)?

sofia: yes — add the checklist. Also leadership asked that we publish the SLO/gating decision matrix in the next 2 weeks. Can someone volunteer to draft the matrix?

ajay: I'll draft the matrix. Plan: initial draft by next Wed, circulate for review, finalize by end of sprint.

kevin: will set up the CI smoke job for Dedicated and sample baseline export.

devon: PR links once done. I'll also update the oncall handoff doc with the tagging flow and link it in the calendar entry.

sofia: Action items recap:
- devon: add Dedicated milestones to release calendar + update oncall handoff doc (due EOD).
- ajay: draft SLO/gating matrix and add rollout_policy defaults (due next Wed).
- kevin: create Dedicated smoke CI job and baseline export (due by end of week).
- maria: review runbook + add product checklist (ongoing).

maria: quick Q — when we say "rollback" do we mean immediate rollback to previous model or switch to degraded routing (lower-capacity variant)?

ajay: preferable to switch to lower-capacity variant or fallback model if available. Immediate rollback is last-resort because it can introduce instability during heavy traffic. Rollback decision tree will be in the SLO matrix.

sofia: thanks all. If you have follow-ups, drop them here or ping me directly. I'll post a short summary in #all-hands and link to the new calendar/runbook once PRs are merged. :thumbsup:
